questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Quem dividiu o território do Brasil em capitanias hereditárias?
questions.answer: O rei de Portugal
questions.hint: O Brasil era colônia de qual país?

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Em que ano começou o sistema de capitanias hereditárias no Brasil?
questions.hint: Foi algumas décadas depois de 1500.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: O que era uma capitania hereditária?
options: Uma grande faixa de terra entregue a um donatário
questions.answer: Uma grande faixa de terra entregue a um donatário
questions.hint: Pense em terra dividida em pedaços.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Como se chamava a pessoa que recebia uma capitania?
questions.answer: donatário
questions.hint: A palavra vem de "doação".

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Por que as capitanias eram chamadas de "hereditárias"?
options: Porque passavam de pai para filho
questions.answer: Porque passavam de pai para filho
questions.hint: Lembre da palavra "herança".

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual era um dos objetivos de Portugal ao criar as capitanias?
options: Ocupar e proteger o território sem gastar muito
questions.answer: Ocupar e proteger o território sem gastar muito
questions.hint: Portugal tinha pouco dinheiro e medo de invasores.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Quem pagava os gastos para colonizar uma capitania?
questions.answer: O próprio donatário
questions.hint: O rei queria economizar.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual foi um motivo de muitas capitanias não terem dado certo?
options: Falta de dinheiro e grande distância de Portugal
questions.answer: Falta de dinheiro e grande distância de Portugal
questions.hint: Pense nos custos e na viagem longa.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Quais capitanias tiveram mais sucesso?
questions.answer: Pernambuco e São Vicente
questions.hint: Uma ficava no Nordeste, a outra no litoral de São Paulo.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: O que produzia a capitania de Pernambuco que a fez prosperar?
questions.answer: Açúcar
questions.hint: Pense nos engenhos.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Por que Portugal criou o Governo-Geral?
options: Para dar o Brasil à Espanha
Para centralizar a administração e ajudar as capitanias
Para proibir a chegada de colonos
questions.answer: Para centralizar a administração e ajudar as capitanias
questions.hint: As capitanias precisavam de um comando unido.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Em que ano foi criado o Governo-Geral no Brasil?
questions.hint: Foi 14 anos depois das capitanias.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual cidade foi fundada em 1549 para ser a primeira capital do Brasil?
questions.answer: Salvador
questions.hint: Fica na Bahia, na Baía de Todos os Santos.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Em qual estado atual fica Salvador?
questions.answer: Bahia
questions.hint: A cidade fica junto à Baía de Todos os Santos.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: As capitanias acabaram quando o Governo-Geral foi criado?
options: Não, as duas formas de organização existiram juntas por muito tempo
questions.answer: Não, as duas formas de organização existiram juntas por muito tempo
questions.hint: O Governo-Geral veio para ajudar, não para substituir de uma vez.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Imagine que você é um donatário recém-chegado. Escreva duas dificuldades que enfrentaria e por que o Governo-Geral poderia ajudar.
questions.hint: Pense em dinheiro, defesa e distância.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What is the headline of a newspaper report?
options: The short title in large letters at the top
questions.answer: The short title in large letters at the top
questions.hint: It is the first thing you notice.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which is the best headline for a report about a lost dog found in a school library?
options: Lost Dog Turns Up in School Library
My favourite animal is a dog
How to look after a pet dog
Once upon a time there was a dog
questions.answer: Lost Dog Turns Up in School Library
questions.hint: Headlines are short and grab attention.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What should the lead (opening) paragraph tell the reader?
options: Who, what, when, where (and often why)
questions.answer: Who, what, when, where (and often why)
questions.hint: Think of the five W questions.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: In which tense are newspaper reports mostly written?
questions.answer: Past tense
questions.hint: The events have already happened.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which sentence is in the past tense?
options: The firefighters will rescue the cat.
The firefighters rescued the cat on Tuesday.
questions.answer: The firefighters rescued the cat on Tuesday.
questions.hint: Look for a verb ending in -ed.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What word do we use for the exact words a person says, written inside inverted commas in a report?
questions.answer: quote
questions.hint: Reporters collect these from witnesses.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which sentence uses inverted commas correctly?
questions.answer: "It was amazing," said Ellie.
questions.hint: Inverted commas go around only the spoken words.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Change to reported speech: "I am very proud," said the coach.
options: The coach said that I am very proud.
The coach said that he was very proud.
The coach says I was proud.
questions.answer: The coach said that he was very proud.
questions.hint: In reported speech, "I am" usually becomes "he was".

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Change to reported speech: "We won the match," said Priya.
options: Priya said that we win the match.
Priya said that they will win the match.
Priya said that they had won the match.
questions.answer: Priya said that they had won the match.
questions.hint: "We" becomes "they" and the tense moves back.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which of these is NOT usually a feature of a newspaper report?
questions.answer: A "happily ever after" ending
questions.hint: Think about stories versus reports.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Why do reporters include quotes from witnesses?
options: To show what people saw and make the report believable
questions.answer: To show what people saw and make the report believable
questions.hint: Quotes add real voices.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which sentence is a fact rather than an opinion?
options: The bridge is the most beautiful in the world.
questions.answer: The bridge opened on 3rd May.
questions.hint: A fact can be checked.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What is a caption in a newspaper?
options: A short sentence under a photo explaining it
questions.answer: A short sentence under a photo explaining it
questions.hint: Look below the picture.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Rewrite in the past tense: "The mayor opens the new park." Write only the verb.
questions.answer: opened
questions.hint: Add the past tense ending.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Write a lead paragraph (2–3 sentences) for a report about a school sports day that was stopped by a sudden hailstorm. Answer who, what, when and where.
questions.hint: Start with the most important information.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Write a headline and one quote from a witness for a report about a giant pumpkin winning a village competition.
questions.hint: Keep the headline short; put the spoken words in inverted commas.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: What is a playscript?
options: A set of instructions for a recipe
A text written to be performed by actors
questions.answer: A text written to be performed by actors
questions.hint: Think of the theatre.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: In a playscript, where is the character's name usually written?
options: On the left, before the words they say
At the bottom of the page
questions.answer: On the left, before the words they say
questions.hint: Playscripts do not use speech marks.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Does a playscript use inverted commas (speech marks) for the characters' lines?
options: No, the name and a colon or a new line show who speaks
questions.answer: No, the name and a colon or a new line show who speaks
questions.hint: Look at how lines are laid out.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: What do we call the instructions in a playscript that tell actors how to move or speak?
questions.answer: stage directions
questions.hint: They are often in brackets or italics.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Which of these is a stage direction?
questions.answer: (Tom tiptoes towards the door.)
questions.hint: It tells the actor what to do, not what to say.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: In which tense are stage directions usually written?
questions.answer: Present tense
questions.hint: They describe what is happening now on stage.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: What is the purpose of a cast list at the start of a playscript?
options: To give the answers to questions
To list the characters in the play
To show the price of tickets
questions.answer: To list the characters in the play
questions.hint: It tells you who is in the play.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: What does "Scene 1" show in a playscript?
options: The start of a part of the play in one place or time
questions.answer: The start of a part of the play in one place or time
questions.hint: Plays are divided into sections.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: A stage direction says "(angrily)". How should the actor read the line?
questions.answer: In a loud, cross voice
questions.hint: The word describes a feeling.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: What does "intonation" mean when reading aloud?
options: How fast you turn the page
The rise and fall of your voice
questions.answer: The rise and fall of your voice
questions.hint: Think about how your voice goes up and down.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: How should your voice usually change at the end of a question like "Are you coming?"
questions.answer: It often rises
questions.hint: Listen to yourself asking a question.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: MAYA: (whispering) Shh! The dragon is asleep. How should Maya say this line?
options: Quietly, as if she is afraid to wake it
questions.answer: Quietly, as if she is afraid to wake it
questions.hint: Look at the stage direction and the situation.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Why do playscripts include stage directions?
options: To help actors and directors know how to perform the scene
questions.answer: To help actors and directors know how to perform the scene
questions.hint: Actors need to know more than just the words.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Which sentence is written in playscript layout?
options: Leo found the map, which was old.
Leo said that he had found the map.
questions.answer: LEO: I found the map!
questions.hint: Look for a name followed by a colon.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Turn this sentence from a story into two lines of playscript, with one stage direction: "Sara shouted at her brother to give back her bike."
questions.hint: Write the character name, a colon and what they say.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Choose one line of dialogue and explain how you would use your voice and body to show a character is nervous.
questions.hint: Think about volume, speed, pauses and movement.
